Getting started with coreval

Source: vignettes/coreval.Rmd
coreval.Rmd

coreval checks SDTM, SEND and USDM data against CDISC’s conformance rules, inside R, on your own machine. This page shows the few steps you need and then answers the questions people ask most. For how it all works underneath, see vignette("technical", package = "coreval").

coreval is a personal open-source project. It is not a CDISC product and is not validated software. Treat its findings as a fast first check, and run your qualified tool before you submit.

Four steps

1. Install and load 

install.packages("coreval")
install.packages(c("xml2", "writexl"))  # optional: define.xml and Excel output
library(coreval)

2. Check a dataset while you write it

Give check_dataset() the data frame you just built. Row 2 below has 2024-02-30, a date that does not exist.

ae <- data.frame(
  STUDYID = "DEMO", DOMAIN = "AE", USUBJID = c("S1", "S1", "S2"),
  AESEQ = c(1, 2, 1), AETERM = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Rash"),
  AESTDTC = c("2024-01-10", "2024-02-30", "2024-01-12"),
  AEENDTC = c("2024-01-12", "2024-02-01", "")
)

result <- check_dataset(ae, standard = "SDTMIG", version = "3.4")
result
#> 
#> ── coreval — AE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> 8 problems across 3 records  (152 checks ran)
#> 
#>   wrong value         2   the data breaks the rule - start here
#>   missing required    4   the standard requires it

#> [wrong value]
#> --STDTC falls after --ENDTC.
#>   1 record · AESTDTC, AEENDTC
#>     row 2  S1 seq 2  AESTDTC = "2024-02-30", AEENDTC = "2024-02-01"

#> 
#> [wrong value]
#> Value must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime or interval.
#>   1 record · AESTDTC

#>     row 2  S1 seq 2  AETERM = "Nausea", AESTDTC = "2024-02-30"

A file works too: check_dataset("ae.xpt", standard = "SDTMIG"), or a .sas7bdat or .csv.

3. Check the whole study

Once the datasets exist as files, point check_study() at the folder. This is the only way to run the rules that compare one dataset with another, such as an adverse event date against the subject’s dates in DM.

result <- check_study("path/to/sdtm", standard = "SDTMIG", version = "3.4")

If the folder holds a define.xml, it is used automatically (with xml2 installed).

4. Save it for the team 

write_findings(result, "issues.xlsx")

The workbook has four sheets: the problems, one row each; the affected records, by subject and sequence number; the checks that could not run, with what to do about them; and every rule with what happened to it. Status and Notes columns are there for you to fill in.

Reading the report

Every problem carries one of three tags:

Tag Means What to do
wrong value the data holds a value that breaks the rule fix it, start here
missing required something the standard requires is absent or blank fix it
missing optional something expected is absent often fine: check whether it applies to your study

The detail is in two tables:

# what is wrong: dataset, row, subject, variable, value
f <- result$findings
head(f[!is.na(f$Record), c("Dataset", "Record", "USUBJID", "SEQ", "Variable", "Value")])
#>    Dataset Record USUBJID   SEQ Variable          Value
#>     <char>  <int>  <char> <num>   <char>         <char>
#> 1:      AE      2      S1     2  AESTDTC     2024-02-30
#> 2:      AE      2      S1     2  AEENDTC     2024-02-01
#> 3:      AE      1      S1     1    EPOCH Not in dataset
#> 4:      AE      2      S1     2    EPOCH Not in dataset
#> 5:      AE      3      S2     1    EPOCH Not in dataset
#> 6:      AE      1      S1     1   AETERM       Headache

# what could not be checked, and why
head(unique(result$skipped$reason), 3)
#> [1] "needs TV, which is not in this study"                                                        
#> [2] "needs SV, which is not in this study"                                                        
#> [3] "evaluation failed: a date is not a real date (2024-02-30), and CORE 1.0 stops the rule on it"

Record is the row in the file. USUBJID and SEQ are the record’s subject and --SEQ, which still find it after the data is sorted; they are blank in a dataset without them, such as TS. Each finding also has the issue in words, its triage and the rule_id. A blank Record means the problem is about the dataset as a whole, such as a missing variable. For a rule about the variables themselves, such as a wrong type or label, Record is the variable’s position in the dataset, not a row, and Variable and Value name the variable.

Always look at skipped. A short list of problems can mean clean data, or it can mean many rules never ran. The skipped table tells you which.

Common tasks

Show me only the real errors 

errors <- filter_findings(result, triage = "wrong value")
errors
#> 
#> ── coreval ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> (filtered - this is a subset of the full result)
#> 
#> 3 problems across 2 records in 2 datasets  (346 checks ran)
#> 
#>   wrong value         3   the data breaks the rule - start here
#> 
#>   AE           2 problems    1 record
#>   DM           1 problem     1 record
#> 
#> ── AE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> [wrong value]
#> --STDTC falls after --ENDTC.
#>   1 record · AESTDTC, AEENDTC
#>     row 2  S1 seq 2  AESTDTC = "2024-02-30", AEENDTC = "2024-02-01"
#>     CORE-000718  · also FB3209
#> 
#> [wrong value]
#> Value must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime or interval.
#>   1 record · AESTDTC
#>     row 2  S1 seq 2  AESTDTC = "2024-02-30"
#>     CORE-002121  · also CG0011
#> 
#> ── DM ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> [wrong value]
#> AGEU must be populated when AGE is populated.
#>   1 record · AGE, AGEU
#>     row 3  S3  AGE = "47", AGEU = (empty)
#>     CORE-000189  · also CG0665
#> 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 81 checks could not run.
#>   21 need datasets this study does not have (CE, DS, EX, RELREC, SS, SUPPDM, ...)
#>   52 need a define.xml
#>      → put it in the study folder (reading it needs the xml2 package)
#>   4 need to know the controlled terminology version
#>      → pass ct_package ("sdtmct-..." or "sendct-..."; see list_ct_packages()), or for a study fill TSVCDREF and TSVCDVER in TS
#>   2 need the study tagging file (stf.xml)
#>      → put it in the study folder
#>   1 need variables the data does not have
#>   1 for other reasons, see result$skipped
#> 
#> Scoped to SDTMIG: 122 rules written for other standards, or other versions of this one, were not run.
#> 
#> Fix what you can, then run this again.
#> To track the rest:  write_findings(result, "issues.xlsx")

You can also narrow by dataset, rule or variable, and save the narrowed result with write_findings(). The saved file notes that it is a subset.

My study is SDTMIG 3.3, or SEND

standard is required, and only the rules for that standard and version run:

check_study("path/to/sdtm", standard = "SDTMIG", version = "3.3")
check_study("path/to/send", standard = "SENDIG", version = "3.1")

Leave version out and the rules for every version of that standard run. list_rules() shows which standards and versions there are.

It says terminology checks were skipped

Rules about allowed values (is SEX one of the permitted terms?) need to know which Controlled Terminology release your study uses. coreval reads it from TSVCDVER in your TS dataset (on rows whose TSVCDREF is CDISC), or from the define.xml. If neither says, tell it:

list_ct_packages("sdtm")   # every release you can choose from
check_study("path/to/sdtm", standard = "SDTMIG", ct_package = "sdtmct-2026-03-27")

Many checks say “was not supplied”

You checked one dataset, and those rules compare it with another one. Run check_study() on the folder that holds both.

Stop my program when a dataset has errors

Put a check at the end of the code that builds a dataset:

r <- check_dataset(ae, standard = "SDTMIG", version = "3.4")
bad <- filter_findings(r, triage = "wrong value")
if (nrow(bad$findings) > 0) {
  print(bad)
  stop("AE has values that break CDISC rules")
}

Find out what a rule checks

The report ends each problem with a rule id. Look it up:

rule <- list_rules(id = "CORE-000718")
rule$issue        # what it checks
#> [1] "--STDTC falls after --ENDTC."
rule$legacy_ids   # the same rule's id in CDISC's Conformance Rules or FDA lists
#> [1] "FB3209"

print(result, guidance = TRUE) adds the Implementation Guide sentence behind each rule to the report.

See every problem, not just the first ten 

print(result, n = Inf)   # every problem in the report
result$findings          # every finding, as a table

A rule that flags a very large number of records keeps the first 1,000 and records the real count in result$truncated. Pass max_records = Inf to keep them all.

Check one file of a split dataset

check_dataset("lb1.xpt", standard = "SDTMIG") reads the domain from the DOMAIN column. If the file has none, say which domain it is with domain = "LB".

Check a big study faster

  • Set version as well as standard: fewer rules run.
  • Read once, check several times:
study <- read_study("path/to/sdtm")
r1 <- check_study(study, standard = "SDTMIG", version = "3.4")

A progress bar shows in interactive sessions. Turn it off with options(coreval.progress = FALSE).

Check a USDM study design

Put the USDM JSON file in a folder of its own and ask for it. It needs the jsonlite and QuickJSR packages, and no standard, since the document is USDM.

check_study("path/to/usdm", usdm = TRUE)

Questions people ask

No problems were found. Is my data clean? Not necessarily. Look at result$skipped first. Checking one dataset on its own leaves out every rule that compares datasets, and the terminology rules need a CT release.

What does Not in dataset mean in the Value column? The rule wanted a variable your dataset does not have. That is usually the finding.

What is a Variable starting with $? Something the rule worked out from your data, such as the list of STUDYID values in DM, shown so you can see what your record was compared against.

A warning says some files were not read. A study folder is read from .xpt, .sas7bdat and Dataset-JSON files. CSV files are skipped there, since they carry no types or labels; check one with check_dataset(). If two files hold the same dataset, the warning says which one was used.

Does anything leave my computer? No. There is no internet access, account or API key. The rules and terminology are bundled in the package.

Which rules version produced my results? attr(list_rules(), "rules_version"). It is also recorded in every file write_findings() saves.

A result looks wrong. Please open an issue, ideally with a small dataset that shows it. A wrong or missing finding is the most useful thing you can report.

All the functions

Function Use it to
check_dataset(x, standard = ) check one data frame or file
check_study(path, standard = ) check a whole study folder
write_findings(result, path) save to Excel or CSV
filter_findings(result, ...) narrow a result
list_rules() look up rules
list_ct_packages() list Controlled Terminology releases
read_study(path) read a folder once, to check it several times
